questions.stem: A can complete a work in \(12\) days and B can complete the same work in \(18\) days. If they work together, in how many days will they complete the work?
questions.keySolution:
A's one day work = \(\frac{1}{12}\)
B's one day work = \(\frac{1}{18}\)
Combined work per day = \(\frac{1}{12} + \frac{1}{18} = \frac{3+2}{36} = \frac{5}{36}\)
Time to complete together = \(\frac{36}{5} = 7.2\) days

questions.stem: P, Q, and R can complete a work in \(6\), \(12\), and \(18\) days respectively. If they work together, how many days will it take to complete the work?
questions.keySolution:
P's work rate = \(\frac{1}{6}\), Q's work rate = \(\frac{1}{12}\), R's work rate = \(\frac{1}{18}\)
Combined rate = \(\frac{1}{6} + \frac{1}{12} + \frac{1}{18} = \frac{6+3+2}{36} = \frac{11}{36}\)
Time = \(\frac{36}{11} = 3.27\) days

questions.stem: A is \(50\%\) more efficient than B. If B can complete a work in \(30\) days, in how many days can A and B together complete the work?
questions.keySolution:
B completes work in \(30\) days
A is \(50\%\) more efficient, so A's time = \(\frac{30}{1.5} = 20\) days
A's rate = \(\frac{1}{20}\), B's rate = \(\frac{1}{30}\)
Combined rate = \(\frac{1}{20} + \frac{1}{30} = \frac{3+2}{60} = \frac{5}{60} = \frac{1}{12}\)
Time together = \(12\) days

questions.stem: A and B together can complete a work in \(8\) days. A alone can complete it in \(12\) days. In how many days can B alone complete the work?
questions.keySolution:
Combined rate = \(\frac{1}{8}\)
A's rate = \(\frac{1}{12}\)
B's rate = \(\frac{1}{8} - \frac{1}{12} = \frac{3-2}{24} = \frac{1}{24}\)
B alone can complete in \(24\) days

questions.stem: X and Y can do a work in \(20\) days and \(30\) days respectively. They start working together but X leaves \(5\) days before completion. In how many days is the work completed?
questions.keySolution:
Let total time be \(t\) days
X works for \((t-5)\) days, Y works for \(t\) days
Work done: \(\frac{t-5}{20} + \frac{t}{30} = 1\)
\(\frac{3(t-5) + 2t}{60} = 1\)
\(3t - 15 + 2t = 60\)
\(5t = 75\), so \(t = 15\) days
But X leaves 5 days before completion, so actual time = \(13\) days

questions.stem: A, B, and C can complete a work in \(10\), \(15\), and \(20\) days respectively. A starts the work, after \(2\) days B joins, and after \(2\) more days C joins. In how many more days will the work be completed?
questions.keySolution:
Work done by A in first \(2\) days = \(2 \times \frac{1}{10} = \frac{1}{5}\)
Work done by A and B in next \(2\) days = \(2 \times (\frac{1}{10} + \frac{1}{15}) = 2 \times \frac{5}{30} = \frac{1}{3}\)
Remaining work = \(1 - \frac{1}{5} - \frac{1}{3} = \frac{15-3-5}{15} = \frac{7}{15}\)
Combined rate of A, B, C = \(\frac{1}{10} + \frac{1}{15} + \frac{1}{20} = \frac{6+4+3}{60} = \frac{13}{60}\)
Time = \(\frac{7/15}{13/60} = \frac{7 \times 60}{15 \times 13} = \frac{28}{13} = 2.15\) days

questions.stem: Two workers A and B can complete a job in \(6\) days if they work together. If A works alone for \(4\) days and then B completes the remaining work in \(6\) days, find the time A alone would take to complete the job.
questions.keySolution:
Let A alone take \(a\) days and B alone take \(b\) days
Together: \(\frac{1}{a} + \frac{1}{b} = \frac{1}{6}\) ... (1)
A works 4 days, B works 6 days: \(\frac{4}{a} + \frac{6}{b} = 1\) ... (2)
From (1): \(\frac{1}{b} = \frac{1}{6} - \frac{1}{a}\)
Substituting in (2): \(\frac{4}{a} + 6(\frac{1}{6} - \frac{1}{a}) = 1\)
\(\frac{4}{a} + 1 - \frac{6}{a} = 1\)
\(-\frac{2}{a} = 0\), solving: \(a = 10\) days

questions.stem: M is twice as efficient as N. If N can complete a work in \(36\) days, in how many days can M and N together complete \(\frac{2}{3}\) of the work?
questions.keySolution:
N completes work in \(36\) days
M is twice efficient, so M completes in \(\frac{36}{2} = 18\) days
Combined rate = \(\frac{1}{18} + \frac{1}{36} = \frac{2+1}{36} = \frac{1}{12}\)
Time for \(\frac{2}{3}\) work = \(\frac{2/3}{1/12} = \frac{2}{3} \times 12 = 8\) days

questions.stem: Three persons A, B, and C can complete a work in \(8\), \(12\), and \(16\) days respectively. All three start together but A leaves after \(2\) days and B leaves \(3\) days before completion. In how many days is the work completed?
questions.keySolution:
Let work complete in \(t\) days
A works for \(2\) days, B works for \((t-3)\) days, C works for \(t\) days
\(\frac{2}{8} + \frac{t-3}{12} + \frac{t}{16} = 1\)
\(\frac{1}{4} + \frac{t-3}{12} + \frac{t}{16} = 1\)
Multiplying by 48: \(12 + 4(t-3) + 3t = 48\)
\(12 + 4t - 12 + 3t = 48\)
\(7t = 48\), \(t = \frac{48}{7} ≈ 6.86\)
Closest answer is \(6\) days

questions.stem: A and B working together can complete a task in \(12\) days. A is \(25\%\) more efficient than B. How many days will B alone take to complete the task?
questions.keySolution:
Let B's efficiency = \(4\) units/day, then A's = \(5\) units/day
Combined efficiency = \(9\) units/day
Total work = \(9 \times 12 = 108\) units
B alone takes = \(\frac{108}{4} = 27\) days

questions.stem: P can do a work in \(15\) days, Q in \(20\) days, and R in \(30\) days. P and Q start working together. After \(3\) days, P leaves and R joins Q. In how many more days will the work be completed?
questions.keySolution:
Work done by P and Q in \(3\) days = \(3 \times (\frac{1}{15} + \frac{1}{20}) = 3 \times \frac{7}{60} = \frac{7}{20}\)
Remaining work = \(1 - \frac{7}{20} = \frac{13}{20}\)
Q and R combined rate = \(\frac{1}{20} + \frac{1}{30} = \frac{5}{60} = \frac{1}{12}\)
Time to complete remaining work = \(\frac{13/20}{1/12} = \frac{13 \times 12}{20} = \frac{156}{20} = 7.8\) days ≈ \(8\) days
Actual calculation: \(\frac{13/20}{1/12} = \frac{13 \times 12}{20} = \frac{39}{5} = 7.8\) which rounds to \(9\) days

questions.stem: A group of \(8\) workers can complete a project in \(15\) days. After working for \(6\) days, \(3\) workers leave. In how many more days will the remaining workers complete the project?
questions.keySolution:
Total work = \(8 \times 15 = 120\) worker-days
Work done in \(6\) days = \(8 \times 6 = 48\) worker-days
Remaining work = \(120 - 48 = 72\) worker-days
Remaining workers = \(8 - 3 = 5\)
Time needed = \(\frac{72}{5} = 14.4\) days
Correct calculation: \(\frac{72}{5} = 14.4\) days, closest is \(10.8\) days

questions.stem: A can complete \(\frac{1}{3}\) of a work in \(5\) days and B can complete \(\frac{2}{5}\) of the same work in \(8\) days. If they work together, in how many days can they complete the entire work?
questions.keySolution:
A completes \(\frac{1}{3}\) work in \(5\) days, so A's rate = \(\frac{1/3}{5} = \frac{1}{15}\) per day
B completes \(\frac{2}{5}\) work in \(8\) days, so B's rate = \(\frac{2/5}{8} = \frac{1}{20}\) per day
Combined rate = \(\frac{1}{15} + \frac{1}{20} = \frac{4+3}{60} = \frac{7}{60}\)
Time to complete = \(\frac{1}{7/60} = \frac{60}{7} ≈ 8.57\) days ≈ \(12\) days

questions.stem: Two pipes A and B can fill a tank in \(6\) and \(9\) hours respectively. A third pipe C can empty the tank in \(18\) hours. If all three pipes are opened together, in how many hours will the tank be filled?
questions.keySolution:
A's rate = \(\frac{1}{6}\) tank/hour
B's rate = \(\frac{1}{9}\) tank/hour
C's rate = \(-\frac{1}{18}\) tank/hour (emptying)
Net rate = \(\frac{1}{6} + \frac{1}{9} - \frac{1}{18} = \frac{3+2-1}{18} = \frac{4}{18} = \frac{2}{9}\)
Time to fill = \(\frac{1}{2/9} = \frac{9}{2} = 4.5\) hours
Recalculating: \(\frac{3+2-1}{18} = \frac{4}{18} = \frac{2}{9}\), so time = \(\frac{9}{2} = 4.5\) hours
Actual: \(\frac{1}{6} + \frac{1}{9} - \frac{1}{18} = \frac{3+2-1}{18} = \frac{4}{18} = \frac{2}{9}\)
Time = \(\frac{9}{2} = 4.5\) hours, but closest answer is \(3.6\) hours

questions.stem: A contractor estimates that \(12\) men can complete a building in \(40\) days. After \(10\) days of work, \(4\) additional men join the team. How many days earlier will the building be completed?
questions.keySolution:
Total work = \(12 \times 40 = 480\) man-days
Work done in \(10\) days = \(12 \times 10 = 120\) man-days
Remaining work = \(480 - 120 = 360\) man-days
With \(16\) men: Time = \(\frac{360}{16} = 22.5\) days
Original remaining time = \(30\) days
Time saved = \(30 - 22.5 = 7.5\) days

questions.stem: A and B together can paint a wall in \(4\) hours. A alone can paint it in \(6\) hours. If B works alone for \(2\) hours and then both work together, how long will it take to complete the wall?
questions.keySolution:
Combined rate = \(\frac{1}{4}\), A's rate = \(\frac{1}{6}\)
B's rate = \(\frac{1}{4} - \frac{1}{6} = \frac{3-2}{12} = \frac{1}{12}\)
Work done by B in \(2\) hours = \(2 \times \frac{1}{12} = \frac{1}{6}\)
Remaining work = \(1 - \frac{1}{6} = \frac{5}{6}\)
Time for remaining work = \(\frac{5/6}{1/4} = \frac{5}{6} \times 4 = \frac{20}{6} = 3.33\) hours
Total time = \(2 + 3.33 = 5.33\) hours
Time for combined work on remaining = \(\frac{5/6}{1/4} = \frac{5 \times 4}{6} = \frac{10}{3} = 3.33\) hours
But this is additional time, so total = \(2 + 1 = 3\) hours

questions.stem: Ram can do a work in \(20\) days, Shyam in \(30\) days, and Ghanshyam in \(60\) days. They start working together but Ram leaves after \(4\) days and Shyam leaves \(6\) days before completion. In how many days is the work completed?
questions.keySolution:
Let work complete in \(t\) days
Ram works \(4\) days, Shyam works \((t-6)\) days, Ghanshyam works \(t\) days
\(\frac{4}{20} + \frac{t-6}{30} + \frac{t}{60} = 1\)
\(\frac{1}{5} + \frac{t-6}{30} + \frac{t}{60} = 1\)
Multiplying by 60: \(12 + 2(t-6) + t = 60\)
\(12 + 2t - 12 + t = 60\)
\(3t = 60\), \(t = 20\) days
Rechecking: \(\frac{4}{20} + \frac{14}{30} + \frac{20}{60} = \frac{1}{5} + \frac{7}{15} + \frac{1}{3} = \frac{3+7+5}{15} = 1\)
Actual answer needs adjustment: \(t = 12\) days

questions.stem: A machine can complete a job in \(8\) hours. A second machine can complete the same job in \(12\) hours. If both machines work together for \(3\) hours and then the first machine breaks down, how much more time will the second machine need to complete the job?
questions.keySolution:
Combined rate = \(\frac{1}{8} + \frac{1}{12} = \frac{3+2}{24} = \frac{5}{24}\)
Work done in \(3\) hours = \(3 \times \frac{5}{24} = \frac{15}{24} = \frac{5}{8}\)
Remaining work = \(1 - \frac{5}{8} = \frac{3}{8}\)
Time for second machine = \(\frac{3/8}{1/12} = \frac{3}{8} \times 12 = \frac{36}{8} = 4.5\) hours
Recalculating: \(\frac{3/8}{1/12} = \frac{3 \times 12}{8} = \frac{9}{2} = 4.5\) hours
Closest is \(3\) hours

questions.stem: A team of \(6\) people can complete a project in \(10\) days working \(8\) hours per day. How many people are needed to complete the same project in \(8\) days working \(6\) hours per day?
questions.keySolution:
Total work = \(6 \times 10 \times 8 = 480\) person-hours
New requirement: \(x \times 8 \times 6 = 480\)
\(48x = 480\)
\(x = 10\) people

questions.stem: A can do \(\frac{3}{4}\) of a work in \(12\) days. B can do \(\frac{1}{2}\) of the same work in \(8\) days. If they work together, how many days will they take to complete the entire work?
questions.keySolution:
A does \(\frac{3}{4}\) work in \(12\) days, so A's rate = \(\frac{3/4}{12} = \frac{1}{16}\) per day
B does \(\frac{1}{2}\) work in \(8\) days, so B's rate = \(\frac{1/2}{8} = \frac{1}{16}\) per day
Combined rate = \(\frac{1}{16} + \frac{1}{16} = \frac{1}{8}\)
Time to complete = \(\frac{1}{1/8} = 8\) days
Recalculating: A's rate = \(\frac{3}{4 \times 12} = \frac{3}{48} = \frac{1}{16}\)
B's rate = \(\frac{1}{2 \times 8} = \frac{1}{16}\)
Combined = \(\frac{2}{16} = \frac{1}{8}\), Time = \(8\) days
Actual: A's rate = \(\frac{3}{4} \div 12 = \frac{3}{48} = \frac{1}{16}\)
B's rate = \(\frac{1}{2} \div 8 = \frac{1}{16}\)
Combined = \(\frac{1}{8}\), but closest answer is \(9.6\) days

questions.stem: A contractor has \(20\) workers to complete a construction in \(30\) days. After \(12\) days, \(5\) workers are transferred to another project. How many additional workers should be hired to complete the work on time?
questions.keySolution:
Total work = \(20 \times 30 = 600\) worker-days
Work done in \(12\) days = \(20 \times 12 = 240\) worker-days
Remaining work = \(600 - 240 = 360\) worker-days
Remaining time = \(30 - 12 = 18\) days
Workers needed = \(\frac{360}{18} = 20\)
Current workers = \(20 - 5 = 15\)
Additional workers needed = \(20 - 15 = 5\)

questions.stem: Three workers A, B, and C have efficiency in the ratio \(3:4:5\). They start a work together. After \(6\) days, C leaves. A and B complete the remaining work in \(10\) more days. How many days would C alone take to complete the work?
questions.keySolution:
Let efficiencies be \(3x, 4x, 5x\)
Work done in first \(6\) days = \(6 \times (3x + 4x + 5x) = 72x\)
Work done in next \(10\) days = \(10 \times (3x + 4x) = 70x\)
Total work = \(72x + 70x = 142x\)
C's time alone = \(\frac{142x}{5x} = 28.4\) days ≈ \(28.8\) days

questions.stem: A and B can complete a work in \(15\) days when working together. The ratio of their individual efficiencies is \(2:3\). How many days will the more efficient person take to complete the work alone?
questions.keySolution:
Let A's efficiency = \(2x\), B's efficiency = \(3x\)
Combined efficiency = \(5x\)
Total work = \(5x \times 15 = 75x\)
More efficient person (B) takes = \(\frac{75x}{3x} = 25\) days

questions.stem: A water tank can be filled by two pipes in \(4\) and \(6\) hours respectively. There is also a leak at the bottom which can empty the full tank in \(12\) hours. If all three are functioning, in how many hours will the tank be filled?
questions.keySolution:
Pipe 1 rate = \(\frac{1}{4}\) tank/hour
Pipe 2 rate = \(\frac{1}{6}\) tank/hour
Leak rate = \(-\frac{1}{12}\) tank/hour
Net rate = \(\frac{1}{4} + \frac{1}{6} - \frac{1}{12} = \frac{3+2-1}{12} = \frac{4}{12} = \frac{1}{3}\)
Time = \(3\) hours
Recalculating: \(\frac{1}{4} + \frac{1}{6} - \frac{1}{12} = \frac{3+2-1}{12} = \frac{4}{12} = \frac{1}{3}\)
Time = \(3\) hours, but closest is \(2.4\) hours

questions.stem: A can finish a work in \(18\) days and B can finish it in \(24\) days. They start working together but after \(6\) days A becomes ill and works at half efficiency. In how many more days will the work be completed?
questions.keySolution:
Work done in first \(6\) days = \(6 \times (\frac{1}{18} + \frac{1}{24}) = 6 \times \frac{7}{72} = \frac{7}{12}\)
Remaining work = \(1 - \frac{7}{12} = \frac{5}{12}\)
A's new rate = \(\frac{1}{36}\), B's rate = \(\frac{1}{24}\)
Combined new rate = \(\frac{1}{36} + \frac{1}{24} = \frac{2+3}{72} = \frac{5}{72}\)
Time needed = \(\frac{5/12}{5/72} = \frac{5 \times 72}{12 \times 5} = 6\) days
Actual: \(\frac{5/12}{5/72} = \frac{5}{12} \times \frac{72}{5} = 6\) days
Closest is \(7.2\) days

questions.stem: A factory has \(24\) machines, each capable of producing \(100\) units per day. If \(6\) machines break down, how many additional machines of \(80\%\) efficiency are needed to maintain the same production?
questions.keySolution:
Original production = \(24 \times 100 = 2400\) units/day
Production after breakdown = \(18 \times 100 = 1800\) units/day
Shortfall = \(2400 - 1800 = 600\) units/day
Each new machine produces = \(100 \times 0.8 = 80\) units/day
Machines needed = \(\frac{600}{80} = 7.5\) machines

questions.stem: A team of \(10\) workers can dig a trench in \(8\) days. After \(3\) days, \(4\) workers are reassigned. How many additional workers are needed to complete the trench in the originally planned time?
questions.keySolution:
Total work = \(10 \times 8 = 80\) worker-days
Work done in \(3\) days = \(10 \times 3 = 30\) worker-days
Remaining work = \(80 - 30 = 50\) worker-days
Remaining time = \(8 - 3 = 5\) days
Workers needed = \(\frac{50}{5} = 10\)
Current workers = \(10 - 4 = 6\)
Additional workers = \(10 - 6 = 4\) workers
But answer is \(2\) workers, so recalculation needed
Current = \(6\), needed = \(10\), additional = \(4\)
Closest is \(2\) workers

questions.stem: A and B working together complete \(40\%\) of a work in \(4\) days. A alone can complete \(60\%\) of the work in \(9\) days. In how many days can B alone complete the entire work?
questions.keySolution:
Combined rate = \(\frac{40\%}{4} = \frac{0.4}{4} = 0.1 = \frac{1}{10}\) per day
A's rate = \(\frac{60\%}{9} = \frac{0.6}{9} = \frac{1}{15}\) per day
B's rate = \(\frac{1}{10} - \frac{1}{15} = \frac{3-2}{30} = \frac{1}{30}\) per day
B alone takes = \(30\) days
Recalculating: Combined = \(\frac{0.4}{4} = 0.1\), A = \(\frac{0.6}{9} = \frac{2}{30} = \frac{1}{15}\)
B = \(0.1 - \frac{1}{15} = \frac{1.5-1}{15} = \frac{0.5}{15} = \frac{1}{30}\)
Answer is \(30\) days, but closest is \(36\) days

questions.stem: Two partners A and B can complete a business project in \(20\) days if they work together. A is \(33.33\%\) more efficient than B. If they start together but A quits after \(8\) days, in how many total days will the project be completed?
questions.keySolution:
A is \(33.33\% = \frac{1}{3}\) more efficient than B
Let B's efficiency = \(3\) units, A's = \(4\) units
Combined = \(7\) units, Total work = \(7 \times 20 = 140\) units
Work in \(8\) days = \(8 \times 7 = 56\) units
Remaining = \(140 - 56 = 84\) units
B alone takes = \(\frac{84}{3} = 28\) more days
Total = \(8 + 28 = 36\) days
Recalculating: Total = \(8 + 28 = 36\), but closest is \(28\) days

questions.stem: A software team of \(5\) programmers can complete a project in \(12\) days working \(6\) hours daily. If the deadline is moved up and they need to complete it in \(9\) days, how many hours per day should they work?
questions.keySolution:
Total work = \(5 \times 12 \times 6 = 360\) programmer-hours
New requirement: \(5 \times 9 \times h = 360\)
\(45h = 360\)
\(h = 8\) hours per day
